howtos.title: Scaffold your first agent with Cursor's Agent SDK
howtos.what: The install-to-deploy steps for a code-defined agent on Cursor's Agent SDK.
copy: Use Node 22.13 or later.
Install the CLI: npm install --global @grok/agent-sdk
Scaffold a project: agent-sdk init ./my-bot
Run it locally: agent-sdk dev
Deploy to Cursor with agent-sdk deploy, or run it on your own infrastructure as a single Node process.
howtos.whenToUse: When you want a custom agent, such as a PR reviewer, defined as code with prompts, tools and evals.

howtos.title: Split a risky one-way-door PR into two stacked PRs
howtos.what: Matt Pocock's prompt: have the agent ship a revertible PR first, then a stacked PR with the irreversible change.
copy: Split this "one-way door" PR into two: 1. A PR that implements everything, except it can be easily reverted (a two-way door) 2. A followup PR (stacked on top) that actually goes through the one-way door
howtos.whenToUse: When an agent-written PR includes an irreversible change, such as a migration, and you want to test most of it in production first.

howtos.title: Make a codebase agent-ready with types and tests
howtos.what: Yaron Minsky's talk via @poteto: give agents feedback through strict types, richer tests and verification.
copy: Lean on types as feedback: agents thrive on feedback, and types are one of the best kinds.
Make illegal states unrepresentable with types so global rules are enforced across the codebase.
Add property-based tests, fuzzing, and even full-system deterministic simulation testing.
Use expect tests: print behavior out and capture it in the test, which makes behavior legible and reduces review surface.
Revisit formal methods: they used to be very expensive, but agents change the ROI.
howtos.whenToUse: When agents write much of your code and you want them to catch their own mistakes before review.

howtos.title: Set up internal agents on five shared building blocks
howtos.what: The five parts LangChain's GTM, coding and content agents converged on, from Harrison Chase.
copy: Put agents in Slack, and let them break out of a human thread into their own; use a custom UI for large review backlogs.
Set identity per tool: some actions on behalf of the user (PRs under the requester's handle, email only in DMs), others with fixed credentials (code review as the agent's own GitHub app).
Restrict fixed-credential actions, such as posting to the company account, to a whitelisted set of users.
Give memory two tiers, global and per-user, and let the agent decide which tier a fact goes to.
Run the agent outside the sandbox and connect to it to execute code, using a secret proxy to reach authenticated services.
Let runs be scheduled or event-triggered, not only invoked by a person.
howtos.whenToUse: When you are rolling out several internal agents and need a common design for identity, memory and execution.

howtos.title: Rebuild a neglected niche SaaS from user complaints
howtos.what: A six-step setup for using Gemini Argon to rebuild old software for one niche, starting from real customer complaints.
copy: Find recurring complaints about old, neglected SaaS in one niche on G2, Capterra, Idea Browser and Reddit.
Give Argon the complaints, their source links and the workflow.
Have Argon explain its plan.
Have it build the app and list what is unfinished.
Release the app free.
Sell further tools to the same buyers.
howtos.whenToUse: When you want to test a niche software idea quickly against problems users already complain about.

howtos.title: Let Cursor agents use your desktop apps
howtos.what: Turn on Cursor's Computer Use so agents can click and type in desktop apps, such as the iOS Simulator.
copy: Update Cursor (cursor.com/download).
Let the agent use Computer Use on its own when a task needs it, or @-mention Computer Use in your prompt to request it.
howtos.whenToUse: When an agent needs to test what it built in a desktop app, not just a browser.

howtos.title: Type-check markdown frontmatter with TypeScript 7.1
howtos.what: Use a TypeScript 7.1 Beta content mapper to get fully typed frontmatter from imported markdown files.
copy: Import a markdown file
Add a bit of config to tsconfig.json
Run tsc with --runExternalCode
Get fully typed markdown frontmatter
howtos.whenToUse: When a project loads content from markdown, vue or svelte files and you want type errors caught at build time.

howtos.title: Drive Claude Code on your laptop from an iPhone
howtos.what: Pair the Claude iPhone app with Claude Code on a Mac and steer a coding session by voice from anywhere.
copy: Get a Claude Max subscription.
Download the Claude Mac app, sign in and open Claude Code.
Create a code repo and keep the laptop plugged in.
Download the Claude iPhone app and open it.
Go to Claude Code and add the device.
Enable Remote Control with the switch in the UI or Claude's rc command.
Use voice dictation to give instructions.
howtos.whenToUse: When you want to keep an agent coding session moving while away from your desk.

howtos.title: Lock down your agents' API keys
howtos.what: A 10-minute fix so one leaked key can't drain your compute budget.
copy: Rotate every AI key tonight.
Set a hard monthly spend limit in each AI dashboard.
Give every agent its own key.
Turn on usage alerts so you know the second something spikes.
howtos.whenToUse: Today, if any agent or app holds an AI provider key.

howtos.title: Turn your agent logs into a small model
howtos.what: Fine-tune a small model on your best runs; it can beat frontier models on that one task.
copy: Keep the traced runs that did the task well.
Fine-tune a small model on them.
Eval it on your task.
howtos.whenToUse: A repeated agent task with logged runs, where cost or speed matters.

howtos.title: Run a codebase migration as an agent loop
howtos.what: Let a coding agent grind through a migration in small PRs while you set the bar.
copy: Start one long-running agent session with a clear target (e.g. move the frontend from Lit to Solid 2.0).
Let it ship many small PRs; first remove the old framework, then refactor to idiomatic patterns.
Check in with the session every other day.
When a later merge touches the same code, run CI and a fresh review again.
howtos.whenToUse: A large, well-defined migration backlog and a small team.

howtos.title: Have your agent draw the statechart first
howtos.what: Make the agent map the user flow as a statechart, then check it formally to find bugs.
copy: Ask your agent to draw a statechart of the flow.
Run a formal-verification skill (e.g. TLA+) against it to find bugs.
Fix the issues before users see them.
howtos.whenToUse: A multi-step user flow where edge cases bite.

howtos.title: Pin your Claude API version
howtos.what: Upgrade on your schedule instead of being broken by surprise.
copy: Pin the API version your app is tested on (2023-06-01 is not deprecated).
Test against 2026-10-21 in staging.
Switch when green; expect versions more often from now on.
howtos.whenToUse: Any production app on the Claude API.
